content.text: {"statements": {"L5.1": {"established": "yes", "quote": "For $f(x)=x+c$ ($c\\ge 0$) the original inequalities become \\[\\sqrt{\\frac{x^2 + (y+c)^2}{2}} \\ge \\frac{x+y+c}{2} \\ge \\sqrt{x(y+c)} ,\\] which are exactly the Quadratic\u2011Mean\u2013Arithmetic\u2011Mean inequality and the Arithmetic\u2011Mean\u2013Geometric\u2011Mean inequality applied to the two positive numbers $x$ and $y+c$.", "note": "Both inequalities verified for all x,y>0 and every c>=0."}, "L5.2": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Put $x = f(y)$ ... the chain collapses to equality: $\\bigl(f(f(y)) + y\\bigr)^2 = 4f(y)^2 .$ Taking square roots (all terms are positive) yields f(f(y)) + y = 2f(y)", "note": "Correct derivation; equivalently g(x+g(x))=g(x), giving arithmetic progressions."}, "L5.3": {"established": "no", "quote": null, "note": "Only g(x) > -x noted; negative differences never excluded, yet V \u2286 {0,c} is asserted from 'at most one positive value'."}, "L5.4": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Suppose $V$ contains two distinct positive numbers $c_1 > c_2 > 0$ ... For large $t$ the inequality is violated \u2013 contradiction. ... the set $\\{n c_1 - m c_2\\}$ is dense in $\\mathbb{R}$ ... the right\u2011hand side of (9) tends to $0$ while the left\u2011hand side tends to $+\\infty$", "note": "Both rational and irrational ratio cases treated completely via inequality (7)."}, "L5.5": {"established": "partial", "quote": "From (11) we immediately obtain $(x-y)^2 > c^2$, hence $|x-y| > c$ ... If $x \\in S_0$, then by (12) we must have $|x - (u + n c)| > c$ ... Hence $S_0 = \\emptyset$.", "note": "Mixed fixed/non-fixed case excluded rigorously, but the dichotomy f(x)\u2208{x,x+c} rests on unproved nonnegativity of g."}}, "S_ref": 1, "notes": "Sufficiency is fully verified (both inequalities, all c>=0). Structural identity and the equal-positive-differences argument are complete. Necessity is nearly complete: Lemma 1, (12) and the covering argument kill the mixed case, but negative values of g = f - x are never ruled out, so V \u2286 {0,c} is unjustified."}
